notes.front: What is high availability?
notes.back: Keeping resources as available as possible when they are needed, whatever disruptions or events occur.
notes.explanation: Uptime, or availability, is one of the two biggest considerations when you build or deploy a cloud application.
notes.example: Like a hospital with backup generators, so the lights stay on even when the mains supply fails.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “High availability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a service-level agreement (SLA)?
notes.back: The agreement that sets out a service’s availability guarantees; in Azure, uptime guarantees depend on the service.
notes.explanation: When you design a solution you need to account for these guarantees.
notes.example: Like a courier’s promise that parcels arrive next day, with the terms written down.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “High availability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is scalability?
notes.back: The ability to adjust resources to meet demand.
notes.explanation: If peak traffic overwhelms your systems, being able to scale means adding resources to handle it.
notes.example: Like a restaurant that can open a second dining room on busy nights and close it when quiet.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Scalability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is vertical scaling?
notes.back: Increasing or decreasing the capabilities of a resource: scaling up or scaling down.
notes.explanation: You change how powerful a resource is, not how many resources you have.
notes.example: Like swapping a small van for a bigger one, instead of hiring a second van.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Vertical scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is horizontal scaling?
notes.back: Adding or subtracting the number of resources: scaling out or scaling in.
notes.explanation: You change how many resources you run, not how powerful each one is.
notes.example: Like opening more tills at a supermarket when queues grow, then closing them again.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Horizontal scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is reliability?
notes.back: The ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function.
notes.explanation: It is also one of the pillars of the Microsoft Azure Well-Architected Framework.
notes.example: Like a railway that reroutes trains round a broken signal and keeps the service running.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Reliability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is predictability, as a cloud benefit?
notes.back: Being able to move forward with confidence, focused on performance predictability or cost predictability.
notes.explanation: Both kinds are heavily influenced by the Microsoft Azure Well-Architected Framework.
notes.example: Like a fixed-price building quote with a guaranteed finish date: you can plan around both.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Predictability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is performance predictability?
notes.back: Predicting the resources needed to give your customers a positive experience.
notes.explanation: It is one of the two focuses of predictability in the cloud.
notes.example: Like a theatre knowing how many ushers it needs for a sold-out show.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Performance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is cost predictability?
notes.back: Predicting or forecasting the cost of cloud spending.
notes.explanation: It is the other focus of predictability in the cloud, beside performance.
notes.example: Like a household budget that forecasts next winter’s heating bill from past meter readings.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Cost”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is manageability, as a cloud benefit?
notes.back: The options for managing cloud computing, in two types: management of the cloud and management in the cloud.
notes.explanation: The training calls both types excellent benefits of cloud computing.
notes.example: Like a smart home: the house runs its own heating schedule, and you can also adjust it from an app.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Azure is a highly available cloud environment with uptime guarantees that depend on {{c1::the service}}.
notes.explanation: Those guarantees form part of the service-level agreements.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “High availability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Apart from handling peaks, what other benefit does scalability bring?
notes.back: You do not overpay: when demand drops you reduce resources, and so reduce costs.
notes.explanation: Because the cloud is a consumption-based model, you pay only for what you use.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Scalability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Scaling out or in can be done either {{c1::automatically or manually}}.
notes.explanation: The training gives both as ways deployed resources can follow a jump or drop in demand.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Horizontal scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When would you scale a virtual machine down vertically?
notes.back: When you find you over-specified it: you lower its processor or memory specification.
notes.explanation: Vertical scaling works in both directions: up for more power, down when less is needed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Vertical scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does the cloud’s decentralised design support reliability?
notes.back: Resources can be deployed in regions around the world, so if one region has a catastrophic event, others keep running.
notes.explanation: You can design applications to take advantage of that global scale automatically.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Reliability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In some cases, what can your cloud environment do for you when a region fails?
notes.back: Shift automatically to a different region, with no action needed on your part.
notes.explanation: The training gives this as an example of the reliability that global scale provides.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Reliability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Performance and cost predictability are both heavily influenced by the Microsoft Azure {{c1::Well-Architected Framework}}.
notes.explanation: A solution built around this framework has predictable cost and performance, the training says.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Predictability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two cloud concepts that support performance predictability?
notes.back: Two of: autoscaling, load balancing, high availability (among others).
notes.explanation: Autoscaling adds resources when demand rises; load balancing shifts traffic away from overloaded areas.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Performance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two things the cloud lets you do that support cost predictability?
notes.back: Two of: track resource use in real time; monitor resources for efficiency; analyse data for patterns and trends.
notes.explanation: Using these, you can predict future costs and adjust resources as needed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Cost”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do templates support governance and compliance in the cloud?
notes.back: They help ensure deployed resources meet your technical standards and regulatory requirements, and let you update resources at scale.
notes.explanation: When standards change, the change can be rolled out across resources together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does cloud-based auditing do for governance?
notes.back: It flags resources that are out of compliance with your baseline and provides mitigation strategies.
notes.explanation: It is one of the cloud features the training lists as supporting governance and compliance.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of attack does the training say cloud providers are typically well suited to handle?
notes.back: Distributed denial-of-service attacks.
notes.explanation: Handling them makes your network more robust and secure.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two things that management of the cloud lets you do?
notes.back: Two of: scale automatically; deploy from templates; replace failing resources automatically; get alerts on configured metrics.
notes.explanation: Management of the cloud is about managing your cloud resources themselves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Management of the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two ways of managing in the cloud?
notes.back: Two of: a web portal, a command line interface, application programming interfaces, or PowerShell.
notes.explanation: Management in the cloud is about how you reach and manage your environment and resources.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Management in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Vertical or horizontal? A developer’s virtual machine is short of memory, so she gives it more memory and processors.
notes.back: Vertical scaling (scaling up).
notes.explanation: Adding processors or memory to one machine increases its capabilities, which is vertical scaling.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Vertical scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Vertical or horizontal? A ticketing site adds eight more virtual machines on the morning a festival goes on sale.
notes.back: Horizontal scaling (scaling out).
notes.explanation: Adding more virtual machines or containers changes the number of resources, which is horizontal scaling.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Horizontal scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After the festival sale, traffic falls sharply. What should the ticketing site do with its extra machines, and what is this called?
notes.back: Remove them: scaling in, which also brings costs back down.
notes.explanation: Scaling in when demand drops means you stop paying for resources you no longer need.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Horizontal scaling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An architect must promise the board a level of uptime for a new Azure-hosted service. Where should she look for Azure’s guarantee?
notes.back: In the service-level agreement (SLA) for each Azure service she uses.
notes.explanation: Azure’s uptime guarantees vary by service and are part of its SLAs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “High availability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A team plans to run a service with an availability target on Azure Spot Virtual Machines. What SLA do Spot machines offer?
notes.back: None: there is no SLA, and no high-availability guarantee, for Spot virtual machines.
notes.explanation: Azure allocates Spot machines when capacity is available, and the documentation states plainly that no SLA covers them.
notes.source: Azure documentation: Azure Spot Virtual Machines, “Azure Spot Virtual Machines”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: When deploying Azure Spot Virtual Machines, Azure will allocate the VMs if there's capacity available, but there's no SLA for these VMs. An Azure Spot Virtual Machine offers no high availability guarantees.

notes.front: A flood takes an entire cloud region offline, but a company’s app keeps serving users from another region. Which cloud benefit is this?
notes.back: Reliability.
notes.explanation: Reliability is recovering from failures and continuing to function, helped by resources spread across regions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Reliability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A finance director uses real-time usage tracking and trend analysis to forecast next quarter’s cloud bill. Which kind of predictability is this?
notes.back: Cost predictability.
notes.explanation: Forecasting cloud spending from tracked use and analytics is cost predictability.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Cost”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A website adds resources automatically during a spike and spreads traffic away from its busiest servers, so customers see steady response times. Which kind of predictability is this?
notes.back: Performance predictability.
notes.explanation: Autoscaling and load balancing are among the concepts that support performance predictability.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud, “Performance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A regulator tightens a standard that hundreds of a bank’s cloud resources must meet. How do cloud governance features help?
notes.back: Templates let the bank update resources at scale; auditing flags any still out of compliance.
notes.explanation: The training says templates help resources meet standards and can update them at scale as standards change.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Management of or in the cloud? Resources are monitored and a failing one is replaced automatically.
notes.back: Management of the cloud.
notes.explanation: Monitoring health and replacing failing resources is managing the resources themselves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Management of the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Management of or in the cloud? An engineer runs a PowerShell script to manage the environment.
notes.back: Management in the cloud.
notes.explanation: PowerShell, a command line, a web portal and programming interfaces are ways you manage the environment.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Management in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Vertical versus horizontal scaling: what changes, and what are the directions called?
notes.back: Vertical: a resource’s capabilities, scaled up or down. Horizontal: the number of resources, scaled out or in.
notes.explanation: More processors or memory is vertical; more virtual machines or containers is horizontal.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud, “Scalability”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Management of the cloud versus management in the cloud: what does each cover?
notes.back: Of: managing the resources, such as autoscaling, templates and alerts. In: how you manage them, such as portal, command line or PowerShell.
notes.explanation: One is what gets managed, the other is the means you use to manage it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud, “Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
